confidence_notes: I made six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Ocho Rios prices. Food and drink figures come from aggregator sites (Numbeo-derived pages, Citycost, Mylifeelsewhere, Exiap, TripBase) and a few undated travel guides. These sources disagree, and some may be dated. Nothing I found gave a current Ocho Rios menu price. Beer was about $2.2 to $4, cappuccino about $2.7 to $4, an inexpensive meal about $10 to $15, and a mid-range dinner for two about $30 to $64. I used a rough tourist-facing level, which is higher than local-bar prices. Cocktail is based on a TripBase average of about $8. No source gave a wine-by-the-glass price, so wine is an estimate based on its usual relationship to beer and cocktails. Accommodation figures are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of the Jamaica north-coast market. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. Hostel supply in Ocho Rios is thin and mostly informal, so hostel and 1-star figures are the least certain. The 3-star figure assumes a non-all-inclusive room rate in a July pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: No close comparable city was used. The basis is Jamaican tourist-corridor pricing (Ocho Rios, Montego Bay, Negril), which is higher than local-market prices in Kingston or rural parishes because of resort-driven demand, plus 10% service and 15% GCT on restaurant bills.
